name: Oranga Tamariki (Ministry for Children) - Caregiving/foster care enquiry
coverage: New Zealand (the form lists 61 Oranga Tamariki sites to choose from)
notes: Form fields read: first name, last name and date of birth (required), ethnicity tick boxes, phone and email (both marked required), nearest Oranga Tamariki site, contact preference (email, phone or mail), how you heard, and an optional box for a second person. The page says you must be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident and that you do not need to be a couple or in a relationship. It says a member of the team will contact you; no time is given. The form sends to a Salesforce web-to-case address. Enquiry is step 1 of 5 on the 'Becoming a caregiver' page. A freephone caregiver line is also published (number not recorded here). Page updated 25 July 2025.

name: Oranga Tamariki - Whānau Care partners enquiry
coverage: New Zealand (Whānau Care partnerships with iwi (tribes) and kaupapa Māori (Māori-led) providers)
notes: The page tells people who want to be a whānau (family) caregiver with a Whānau Care partner to phone the Oranga Tamariki caregiver line; Oranga Tamariki then works out whether a partner would be a good fit. Partners named on Oranga Tamariki pages include Waitomo Papakāinga and Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu (see their rows). No list of all partners was found. Page updated 13 February 2023.

name: Oranga Tamariki - Adoption enquiry (domestic and intercountry adoption)
coverage: New Zealand (adoption in New Zealand, intercountry adoption through the New Zealand Central Authority, surrogacy adoption and adoption information)
notes: Form fields read: first name and last name (required), contact preference, phone (required), email, location (16 regions or 'From overseas'), and what you want to know about (for example adopting in New Zealand, intercountry programmes, IVF surrogacy adoption). No reply time stated. The adoption pages say the next step is a group information session. A freephone adoption line is also published (number not recorded here). Oranga Tamariki's chief executive is the New Zealand Central Authority for Hague intercountry adoption. Form page published 21 August 2024.

name: Govt.nz - Fostering a child (caregiving)
coverage: New Zealand
notes: Information row: the national government information site signposts to Oranga Tamariki pages and its caregiving enquiry form. It takes no enquiries itself. Last updated 5 August 2020.

name: Govt.nz - Adopting a child
coverage: New Zealand
notes: Information row: states who can apply (age rules) and signposts to Oranga Tamariki adoption pages, its freephone and its adoption enquiry form. It takes no enquiries itself. Last updated 31 January 2024.

name: Caring Families Aotearoa - Becoming a Caregiver
coverage: New Zealand (lists caregiver recruiters by region)
notes: Information row: national caregiver support organisation (trading name of the New Zealand Family and Fostercare Federation, formerly Fostering Kids New Zealand). It does not recruit caregivers. The page says caregivers can be married, partnered or single, working or at home, owners or renters, and that applying usually takes two to three months. It lists Oranga Tamariki and non-government recruiters by region. Page metadata dated 2025-11-20.

name: Open Home Foundation (Te Whare Kaupapa Awhina) - Foster For Us
coverage: New Zealand (local offices shown on a map that the project's reader could not read)
notes: Christian child and family service. Form fields read: a required tick box to confirm you have read its Special Character Statement, name, email, phone, location or region, and comments or questions (all required). No reply time stated. The page lists the steps: application form, interviews, Police check (including boarders and other adults over 17), medical check, Oranga Tamariki record check, references and a home safety check, then 21 hours of induction training. Listed as nationwide on the Caring Families Aotearoa page. A directory listing seen in search results says 14 centres (unverified). Page metadata dated 2026-04-07.

name: CCS Disability Action - Become a foster carer
coverage: New Zealand (a volunteering listing seen in search results names the Wellington area)
notes: Foster care for disabled children. The site's robots.txt disallows the project's reader, so the page was not opened. Per search extract, anyone over 20 who is a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident can apply, single people can foster and there is no upper age limit. Also listed as nationwide on the Caring Families Aotearoa page. Form not seen.

name: Ngāpuhi Iwi Social Services (NISS) - Mātua Atawhai (caregivers)
coverage: Te Tai Tokerau (Northland); office in Kaikohe
notes: Mātua atawhai are approved caregivers for mokopuna (children) and taitamariki (young people). The page lists emergency care, respite care and care for taitamariki on remand (typically six to eight weeks), and links a Typeform for the mātua atawhai process (form not opened). NISS states it holds Level 1 Social Sector Accreditation (Te Kāhui Kāhu). Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page as an iwi service in Kaikohe.

name: Waitomo Papakāinga - Whānau Care (Te Hiku o Te Ika)
coverage: Kaitaia and Te Hiku o Te Ika (the Far North)
notes: Kaupapa Māori (Māori-led) organisation and an Oranga Tamariki Whānau Care partner since January 2020 (Oranga Tamariki news, 28 January 2020). It connects mokopuna (children) who whakapapa (are descended from) the five iwi of Te Hiku with kaitiaki whānau (caregivers with family connections) and accepts referrals from the Oranga Tamariki Kaitaia site. Oranga Tamariki asks people interested in a Whānau Care partner to contact it first. Own website not found. Oranga Tamariki page published 17 October 2023.

name: Kia Puāwai (formerly Youth Horizons) - Become a caregiver
coverage: Te Tai Tokerau (Northland), Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Waikato, Tauranga Moana (Bay of Plenty) and Te Matau a Māui (Hawke's Bay); Caring Families Aotearoa also lists a South Island office (not confirmed on the agency's site)
notes: Therapeutic foster care using the Teaching-Family Model. Interest form fields read: spare room (yes/no), open to a young person living with you, region (five listed), whether the household is comfortable with Police and Oranga Tamariki vetting ('clean slate does not apply'), how you heard, name, email, phone, street address, city and a free-text box. No reply time stated. The page says a placement is typically a full year; some caregivers offer shorter stays or respite of one to two weeks. The contact form also has a 'Foster carer enquiry' subject. Registered charity.

name: Key Assets New Zealand - Register your interest
coverage: Auckland, Waikato and Bay of Plenty, and Christchurch areas (offices in Auckland, Hamilton and Christchurch)
stated_response_time: we'll get back to you shortly
notes: The page asks people to fill in their details, but no form was in the page the reader received (it may load by script), and the page showed placeholder text. 'Who can foster?' lists: New Zealand citizen or permanent resident; living in the Auckland, Waikato/Bay of Plenty or Christchurch areas; a spare bedroom in the main house. Part of the Key Assets Group, which its site links to the Martin James Foundation; non-profit status in New Zealand not checked. Listed as nationwide on the Caring Families Aotearoa page.

name: Barnardos Aotearoa - Foster care
coverage: Auckland per Caring Families Aotearoa (caregiver recruitment, Royal Oak); the same list names respite services in Whangārei and respite caregiver recruitment in Levin
notes: The foster care page has a short introduction and links to carer stories; an impact story links to it as 'Become a foster caregiver with Barnardos'. No foster care enquiry form or route was found; the 'Get in touch' page lists 17 regional offices. Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa 'Becoming a Caregiver' page (read 2026-11-25; page metadata dated 2025-11-20), which may be out of date.

name: Reconnect Family Services (Te Ope Pirita) - Care & Therapy caregivers
coverage: Auckland and Waikato
notes: Specialised placements for young people in its Care & Therapy programme, with one-to-one whānau (family) or non-kin caregivers. Whānau caregivers are first identified by Oranga Tamariki; then Reconnect's caregiver coordinator makes contact. The programme page gives a phone and email contact for caregivers and social workers. Training listed: a one-day induction and two-day Crisis Prevention Institute training. Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa 'Becoming a Caregiver' page (read 2026-11-25; page metadata dated 2025-11-20), which may be out of date.

name: Immerse
coverage: Auckland (areas served not confirmed)
notes: Listed under Auckland on the Caring Families Aotearoa page (read 2026-11-25). The agency's own site disallows the project's reader in robots.txt, so it was not opened. Search extracts describe a not-for-profit founded by caregivers, with a programme placing a mother and baby with foster parents (unverified). Form not seen.

name: Te Iwi o Ngāti Kahu Trust
coverage: Auckland (Caring Families Aotearoa lists Papatoetoe; the iwi site lists a Tāmaki office)
notes: Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page for iwi caregiver recruitment and training. The link given there returned 404. The Ngāti Kahu iwi home page shows 'TIONK' in its menu and a Tāmaki office, but no caregiver page was found. Whether the trust still recruits is unverified.

name: Homes of Hope Charitable Trust
coverage: Tauranga
notes: Provides homes where brothers and sisters in care can stay together, cared for by live-in house parents and support caregivers (FAQ page). No caregiver enquiry page or form was found. Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa 'Becoming a Caregiver' page (read 2026-11-25; page metadata dated 2025-11-20), which may be out of date.

name: Tūranga Social Services (Te Rūnanga o Tūranganui a Kiwa) - Iwi Maatua Whangai care
coverage: Tūranga (Gisborne)
notes: The site's robots.txt disallows the project's reader, so the page was not opened. Per search extract, the Iwi Maatua Whangai (foster care) service works with Oranga Tamariki to provide short- or long-term care for mokopuna (children) and keeps caregivers trained. Page undated. Form not seen.

name: Ngāti Kahungunu Iwi Incorporated - Te Ara Mātua
coverage: Hawke's Bay (hub in Heretaunga (Hastings); a Napier hub reported in search results)
notes: A Hawke's Bay Today article (modified 22 September 2020) reports that up to 50 people answered the iwi's call for foster and whāngai (customary foster) caregivers. The Te Ara Mātua page was also read: an iwi-led programme with Oranga Tamariki whose hub offers care, health, home and youth support; it shows no caregiver enquiry route. Whether the iwi recruits caregivers now is unverified.

name: Across (Palmerston North)
coverage: Palmerston North (areas served not confirmed)
notes: Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page for caregiver recruitment and training in Palmerston North. The agency's own site disallows the project's reader in robots.txt, so it was not opened. Operator type assumed non-profit (unverified). Form not seen.

name: Kōkiri Marae - whānau caregivers
coverage: Hutt Valley
notes: Oranga Tamariki news (3 October 2025): the marae has its own pool of caregivers for children in Oranga Tamariki care, including respite caregivers, recruits mostly by word of mouth and is looking for more. Oranga Tamariki funds its trauma-informed caregiver training (Matua Rautia). Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page for whānau caregiver recruitment. The marae's own site showed no caregiver page.

name: Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira (Ngāti Toa) - mātua whāngai care
coverage: Porirua and the Wellington region
notes: Oranga Tamariki news (3 October 2025): through its mātua whāngai (customary foster care) arrangement the iwi places children in care with extended whānau (family), is also trying to recruit caregivers who are not next of kin, and has a social worker for its caregivers. It works with the Oranga Tamariki Porirua office. The iwi home page lists Ora Toa Social Services but no caregiver page.

name: Homebuilders West Coast Trust - respite caregivers
coverage: Westport (areas served not confirmed)
notes: Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page for respite caregiver recruitment and training. The agency's own site disallows the project's reader in robots.txt, so it was not opened. Form not seen.

name: Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu - Whānau Care
coverage: Ngāi Tahu mokopuna (children) in care; the Tiaki Taoka model sits alongside Te Kāika in Ōtepoti (Dunedin), Otago
notes: Oranga Tamariki page (5 October 2023): Ngāi Tahu is a Whānau Care partner and recruits whānau (family), hapū (subtribe) and iwi (tribe) caregivers for Ngāi Tahu mokopuna. No direct enquiry route was seen; Oranga Tamariki asks people interested in a Whānau Care partner to contact it first. Region set to Canterbury as the iwi's main base (unverified). Iwi website not opened.

name: Anglican Family Care - Caregiving and Respite Care
coverage: Dunedin (service); offices across Otago
notes: The services page says emergency, short-term or respite care for children from birth to 17 is part of its Dunedin Home-based Family Support service. No caregiver enquiry route was found. Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa 'Becoming a Caregiver' page (read 2026-11-25; page metadata dated 2025-11-20), which may be out of date.

name: Family Works Southland (Presbyterian Support Southland) - Foster Care
coverage: Southland (office in Invercargill)
notes: The page invites people to get in touch by email or phone. It says foster parents may be single, de facto or married, with or without children, and that acceptance after initial training depends on checks, a home visit and an interview. It cares for children in Oranga Tamariki care under contract and also provides community foster care. Listed on the Caring Families Aotearoa page.

name: Adoption First Steps (AFS)
coverage: New Zealand (intercountry adoption from Chile, India, Lithuania, the Philippines and Thailand)
notes: Charitable trust accredited to educate intercountry adoption applicants and do assessments and Home Study reports (Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre). Contact form fields read: name, email (required) and message. The page also links to registration to begin the process and book an education workshop (not opened). Applicants must be New Zealand permanent residents or citizens living and working in New Zealand. The home page says the 2025 international adoption suspension does not affect its process.

name: Inter-Country Adoption New Zealand (ICANZ)
coverage: New Zealand (placement agency for Thailand, India, the Philippines and Lithuania); office in Auckland
notes: Accredited placement agency (Oranga Tamariki Practice Centre). Applicants must first be approved by the New Zealand Central Authority after assessment by AFS or Oranga Tamariki. The contact page gives phone, email and postal details; no form. Registered charity.

name: Compassion for Orphans (CfO)
coverage: New Zealand (placement agency for specific Hague Convention countries)
notes: Named by Oranga Tamariki as an accredited agency that can help place children from overseas. Its own site disallows the project's reader in robots.txt, so it was not opened. Search extracts of Oranga Tamariki factsheets name Chile and Thailand. Operator type assumed non-profit (unverified). Form not seen.
